ai.narrative: No AI-use disclosure established from inspected evidence; non-use is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: Checked current catalogue, source and decision URLs and related titles. Ciaran Anscomb's observation-based rewrite for Dragon/CoCo, with asm6809 build and released source archives. Code is MIT; derived BBC graphics/music/level assets are explicitly excluded from that grant.

sources.reason: OCS/ECS assembly engine with Tiled conversion pipeline, BOBs, ProTracker playback and rewind code. Author targets A500/A600/A2000 with Chip plus Fast RAM; baseline performance claims were not tested.
Direct-hardware A500 engine source; inspected Engine.c contains custom-chip access, bitmap/sprite state and input setup, with PTPlayer assembly.
Small Amiga Intuition board/graphics prototype with object movement and collision code. Main runs a fixed 200-frame demonstration; not presented as a finished game.

3DO executable reconstruction using original executable/debug symbols, intentionally enhanced with timing, scene controls and audio changes. Author explicitly says this is not preservation-level matching.
SDL/CMake engine and editor for a Lost Vikings fan project. README identifies missing supplementary files and old build dependencies; a complete playable release is not established.
Annotated X-Terminator 2.1 cartridge firmware with device RAM structures, scanner state, code format and optional English font. Game accessory firmware, not a game.

Emulicious-derived Columns sound-engine listing with voice/channel structures, PSG registers and envelope/vibrato annotations. Remaining unknown flags are explicit; distinct from full SMS Columns disassembly.
Commented Mark Cooksey engine/data disassembly with WLA-DX integration. Author reports matching audio data, not a playable full game; separate voice sample routine is not covered.
Early WLA-DX disassembly for US/EU Sonic Blast; ROM-splitting and build scripts exist. Japanese G Sonic support remains prospective.
CDL-guided ca65 disassembly tooling implemented in Lua and Notepad++ scripts. README pins tested editor/plugin versions and warns newer versions may fail.
Trax-derived Zelda II listing packaged with ca65/ld65 build scripts and CHR extraction; original disassembly attribution is retained.
Regional NES/Famicom disassembly with Japanese and English asset splitting and NES2 output. Separate from SNES Mother 2; user-supplied ROMs required.
ca65 reassemblable listing guided by Mesen CDL. README explicitly documents ambiguous code/data and limited semantic annotation; exact reconstruction is not equivalent to full understanding.
ca65 source for original NTSC and revision A, with asset extraction and make-test comparison; distinct from tracked game-specific recompilation.
Author-released Jaguar puzzle-game source with game/core libraries and resources. Most levels and webcode generation are deliberately omitted.

Modernized historical Club Drive source supplemented by retail-ROM recovery of missing files. README discloses leaked-source lineage and LLM assistance; source presence does not establish redistribution rights.
Historical Small C, assembler, tools, window library and VAL linker sources, with original notices and build relationships. One coherent compiler-toolchain collection.
Source-based improvement of the author's BBC Manic Miner disassembly, with rendering, timing, collisions, music and Master compatibility changes.
BBC Jet Set Willy disassembly-derived enhancements, including relocated consolidated source, graphics/music corrections and documented crash fixes.
C# reconstruction/visualization of Exile's world-generation algorithms and original map data, derived from Tom Seddon's analysis. Explicitly not a full game.
Unfinished 1993 BBC Micro game by Rich Talbot-Watkins and Matt Godbolt, preserved as original disk and decoded/combined source. Inspected AllSource includes BASIC-hosted assembly.
W.R. Hutsell's VGA strategy game source modernized from QuickBASIC/PDS to QB64. README treats Mac/Linux support as theoretical; only documented Windows target retained.
1995 DOS source with modern compatibility layer and Zig build recipes. README distinguishes compilation success from incomplete SDL/audio and potentially crashing stub runtime.
Author's text-based DOS RPG source including WILD.BAS and story/data files. Development requests and unfinished features remain explicit.
Portable C Atari 2600/7800 disassembler with tracing, hardware labels, configuration overrides and optional cycle comments. Bank-switching/file-size limits remain documented.
Annotated 6809 analysis, graphics decoding and Python tooling for Ken Kalish's game, alongside a Pytch adaptation. Author documents unresolved illegal-opcode behaviour and other uncertainties.

Ciaran Anscomb's observation-based rewrite for Dragon/CoCo, with asm6809 build and released source archives. Code is MIT; derived BBC graphics/music/level assets are explicitly excluded from that grant.
Modern Go/Ebitengine library inspired by fantasy consoles. README explicitly targets modern hardware; an Amiga search hit is not an Amiga engine.
Recursive tree contains only README, licence and gitignore. No game source implementation is present despite the project description.
README explicitly pivots to whole-program ARM60 static recompilation with a Portfolio/3DO runtime. Hold for game-specific recompilation audit rather than label recovered high-level source.
Two BASIC listings have machine-code USR entry points but no README, provenance or corresponding machine-code source. Source completeness/lineage needs clarification.
